Duke will play St. John's at 7:10 p.m. ET on Friday, March 27th, at Capital One Arena in Washington, D.C.It's the second game Duke will be playing at the arena this season, having beaten Michigan, 68-63, in D.C. on February 21st.What channel is Duke vs St. John's game on? Duke vs. St. John's will be the opening game in Friday's slate, and will be broadcast on CBS.Duke vs St. John's prediction St. John's is the healthier team on paper, and certainly looked impressive in the opening weekend. The rehabilitation of Patrick Ngongba and the status of Caleb Foster leaves Duke more vulnerable than the Blue Devils were mid-season. And, of course, St. John's is led by the legendary Rick Pitino - making the Red Storm a popular upset pick this weekend.At the same time, this is a St. John's team that, excluding a back-and-forth series with UConn, didn't appear to be a serious March Madness contender earlier in the season. The Red Storm opened the season 9-5 and lost to the only ranked opponents they faced that aren't the UConn Huskies. They scored two wins over UConn, but also suffered a 32-point blowout in the middle of that three-game series.Ngongba may not have had his midseason form, but he was a difference-maker against TCU. His presence in the paint forces opposing teams to adapt, and even if he plays limited minutes and racks up fouls, it's a value to Duke that those fouls won't be going to Cam Boozer.We saw a much better defensive showing from the Blue Devils in the round of 32, and I don't think there will be any motivation issues like we saw in the first round. Duke is the better team that has passed far more tests than St. John's this season, and the Blue Devils move on.Duke vs St. John's odds Point spread: Duke -6.5Point total: 141.5Moneyline: Duke -290 | St. John's +235Duke basketball injury updates Patrick Ngongba returned against TCU, and while coach Jon Scheyer will still certainly be careful with his rehab and minute-load in the next round, he's expected to play.Scheyer gave a major update on the status of Caleb Foster on Monday, saying he has an "outside shot" of playing against St. John's, as reported by Jon Rothstein. Foster has been out of action and in a walking boot since March 7th, after suffering a fractured foot during Duke's win over the Tar Heels.It was initially expected that Foster may only have a chance to play should Duke make it to the Final Four. The '91, '92, '01, '10 and '15 title teams all bested St. John's at some point during their year.
